contentHtml:
USA – Setara Biosciences has raised US$90 million in Series A financing to advance a pipeline of genetics-based medicines for rare diseases, following Jazz Pharmaceuticals’ acquisition of Actio Biosciences and its lead drug candidate.

The clinical-stage biotechnology company was established after Jazz completed its acquisition of Actio’s lead programme, ABS-1230, an investigational treatment for KCNT1-related epilepsy.

Setara will develop Actio’s remaining portfolio, led by STAR-0871, a clinical-stage small-molecule inhibitor of the TRPV4 ion channel, alongside earlier-stage discovery programmes.

The financing attracted existing investors Deerfield Management, Canaan, Droia Ventures, EcoR1, Euclidean Capital and Regeneron Ventures.

Jazz Pharmaceuticals also joined as a new shareholder following the Actio transaction.

Genetics-based drug development

Setara will use human genetics to identify disease mechanisms and develop small-molecule medicines that target the underlying causes of illness.

Its strategy begins with rare diseases, where genetic evidence can provide insights into disease biology, before applying those findings to more prevalent conditions with similar biological pathways.

David Goldstein, PhD, co-founder, president and executive chair of Setara, said the company would build on Actio’s genetics-driven drug development model while advancing treatments for patients with significant unmet medical needs.

He noted that ABS-1230 would continue development under Jazz, while Setara would focus on the remaining pipeline.

STAR-0871 leads clinical development

Setara’s lead candidate, STAR-0871, formerly ABS-0871, is an oral TRPV4 inhibitor being developed for TRPV4-related neuromuscular disorders, including Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2C (CMT2C), as well as overactive bladder.

CMT2C is a rare inherited condition that affects motor and sensory functions, with approximately 2,500 people affected in the US.

The disease results from gain-of-function mutations in the TRPV4 gene, which cause excessive activity of the associated ion channel.

STAR-0871 is designed to selectively inhibit this channel and address the underlying disease mechanism.

The company is also exploring the drug’s potential in overactive bladder, a condition affecting tens of millions of Americans.

Current treatments have limitations, creating opportunities for therapies that target different biological pathways.

Setara has completed the healthy volunteer portion of a Phase 1 clinical trial of STAR-0871. It plans to begin a Phase 1b study, known as THERON, in patients with CMT2C in 2027.

The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted the candidate Rare Pediatric Disease, Orphan Drug and Fast Track designations.

Separately, the company plans to initiate a Phase 2a trial in patients with overactive bladder.

Beyond STAR-0871, Setara is advancing early-stage discovery programmes targeting genetic epilepsies and potential additional indications, including migraine.

Leadership and investment strategy

Goldstein will lead Setara while retaining his position at Jazz at least until the submission of the new drug application for ABS-1230 for KCNT1-related epilepsy.

Other members of Actio’s leadership team will also join Setara, bringing experience in human genetics, drug discovery and clinical development.

Jason Fuller, PhD, a Setara board member and partner at Deerfield Management, said Actio’s acquisition by Jazz demonstrated the potential of genetics-led drug development.

He added that Deerfield would support Goldstein and the team as they advance STAR-0871 and develop treatments for diseases with significant unmet medical needs.
